{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"Mara kept her palm flat. The knock came again, so gently that she might have mistaken it for the beat of her own heart.

Kit leaned across the aisle. “Is someone there?”

The napkin went cold. From the hole came Gran’s voice, small as a voice heard through a wall: “Not someone. A place.”

Outside, the bridge had vanished. The bus passed shuttered houses standing ankle-deep in the river. At every window, a bowl sat upside down.

Lina looked toward the wheel. “The driver left the key.”

“He had to,” Mara said, though she did not know why until she looked at the napkins in their hands. Each was folded into a neat square. Each bore a name written in Gran’s cramped blue ink. Lina. Kit. Mara. The fourth, pinned beneath Mara’s palm, was blank.

The shape at the wheel lifted its hand again. This time Mara saw a key hanging where its fingers ought to be.

“Ask it to stop,” Kit whispered.

Mara shook her head. Through the dark window of its face, she could still see Gran’s kitchen. The empty chair had begun to slide away from the table, leaving a wet track across the tiles.

Mara took the pen from her coat pocket. It was the one Gran used for shopping lists; she had borrowed it that morning. Holding the napkin down with one hand, she wrote DRIVER across its corner.

The bus stopped so suddenly that all three children pitched forward. The key struck the floor with a bright, ordinary sound. At the wheel sat an empty, dry uniform, and the door folded open onto the bridge."}
